# UX/UI Agent Skills

> A kit of structured instructions, DTCG design tokens, component specs and
> runnable skills that turns Claude into a senior design architect. It targets
> any framework and any design system, and it enforces WCAG 2.2 with gates that
> exit non-zero rather than with advice.

Install with `npx ux-ui-agent-skills init`, open the folder in Claude Code, and
`CLAUDE.md` loads on its own. There is no build step, no dependency and no
runtime: the kit is instructions and knowledge, not a library you import.

## What it ships

- 13 DTCG token files on a three-tier architecture: primitive, semantic, component
- 50 component specs from atoms to templates, each with the eight states and an accessibility spec
- 16 framework adapters plus an Adapter Protocol that generates one on demand
- 138 brand-grade design systems, from Apple and Stripe to Linear and Vercel
- 17 runnable skills invoked as slash commands
- 37 objective gates run as one all-or-nothing command

## Key facts

- Licence: MIT
- Current release: v2.5.1
- Repository: https://github.com/plugin87/ux-ui-agent-skills
- Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/ux-ui-agent-skills
- Requires: Claude Code or any Claude-powered IDE. No Node or Python runtime dependency for the kit itself; the optional gate scripts use python3 and node.
- Accessibility floor: WCAG 2.2 Level AA, with an AAA upgrade path documented
- Dark mode: works by swapping semantic tokens, primitives never move

## Pages

- [Home](https://skills.designlazyyy.com/): what the kit does, how to use it, the design-system library
- [Inside the kit](https://skills.designlazyyy.com/about): the skills, the gates and every layer the kit ships

## How to use it

1. `npx ux-ui-agent-skills init` in the project folder
2. Open the folder in Claude Code
3. Ask in plain words, for example "design a notification component with every state and its accessibility spec"

Skills can also be named directly: `/brandkit`, `/redesign`, `/image-to-code`,
`/a11y-audit`, `/apply-aesthetic`, `/critique`, `/design-tokens`,
`/design-component`, `/design-code`, `/design-review`, `/ux-writing`,
`/token-build`, `/migrate-design-system`, `/prototype`, `/governance`,
`/design-qa`, `/performance`.

## What it does not claim

The gates prove objective correctness: token validity, contrast, state coverage,
keyboard operability, responsive behaviour. They do not prove taste. The kit says
so out loud and ships `/critique`, an adversarial reviewer, for the half no
script can score. A passing gate is never evidence of taste.
